```{r}
library(gt)
library(tidyverse)
library(maps)

#I have read the csv file and viewed it in R
bird_breeding_sites <- read_csv("data/breeding_site_locations.csv")
gt(bird_breeding_sites)

#Use colnames to view just column names
colnames(bird_breeding_sites)

#Use glimpse to see a summary of the table
glimpse(bird_breeding_sites)

#<chr> or <dbl> refers to character or numeric data in the column

#nrow or ncol can be used to see number of rows or columns. dim can be used to see both the dimensions

print(ncol(bird_breeding_sites))
print(nrow(bird_breeding_sites))
print(dim(bird_breeding_sites))

bird_migration_sites <- read_csv("data/migratory_connectivity_dataset.csv")

#only want to see first 10 rows so use head function

gt(head(bird_migration_sites))
glimpse(bird_migration_sites)

#100 rows and 34 columns. Tag is CHR and Birth is DBL

bird_breeding_useful <- bird_breeding_sites |> select(Site, Longitude, Latitude) |> distinct()
gt(bird_breeding_useful) 

#distinct ensures that no duplicate rows are selected


input_vec <- c(5,-10,4,-3)

print(input_vec |>
mean() |>
abs() |>
round())

#performed a series of operations on the set of numbers above using pipe

Y <- 12
Y == 7
Y < 15
Y > 20
Y <= 12

#performed a series of comparison operations on Y
```
